title: Proteomic analysis of phosphorylation, lysine acetylation and total protein changes across differentiating human muscle cells (TMT10plex).
projectDescription: We have carried out proteomic analysis of phosphorylation, lysine acetylation and protein abundance changes across a 6 day time course of human myoblasts differentiating into myotubes in cell culture.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Muscle Differentiation: KM155C25 cells, an immortalized human satellite cell line, were initially incubated in growth medium (4:1 (v/v) Dulbecco’s modified Eagle’s medium with GlutaMAX (DMEM) (glucose 4.5 g/L) : Medium 199 with GlutaMAX (glucose 1.0 g/L) supplemented with 20% fetal bovine serum (FBS), 0.5% penicillin/streptomycin, 25 µg/mL fetuin, 5 ng/mL hEGF, 0.5 ng/mL bFGF, 5 µg/mL insulin and 0.2 µg/mL Dexamethasone), in a 37°C, humidity-saturated incubator, under 95% (v/v) air and  5% (v/v) CO2 until 70% confluence was achieved. Cells were then differentiated into myoblasts using differentiation medium (serum-free DMEM (4.5 g/L glucose) supplemented with 0.5% penicillin/streptomycin and 10 µg/mL insulin) [PMID: 22040608]. Cells were harvested across 6 time points; during proliferation (Day -1; D-1), and five time points starting immediately following the induction of differentiation (Day 0, 1, 2, 3, 4; D0, D1, D2, D3, D4). Biological replicates were collected in triplicate with cells lysed in “one-pot” lysis buffer (PMID: 30159003)  (50 mM triethylammonium bicarbonate (TEAB), pH 8.0, 1% SDC, 10 mM TCEP, 40 mM chloroacetamide), in the presence of protease inhibitors (cOmplete, EDTA-free Protease Inhibitor Cocktail, Roche, Basel, Switzerland) and phosphatase inhibitors (PhosSTOP, Roche), followed by tryptic digestion using a FASP-based approach (PMID: 19377485).  Peptide Labelling: Following digestion, 100 µg aliquots of peptide from each sample, in addition to two mixed control samples comprised of approximately equal contribution from each sample, were labelled with TMT (Thermo Scientific, San Jose CA) according to manufacturer’s instructions. Samples were split across two TMT 10plex experiments as follows: (1) 126 – D-1a, 127N – D-1b, 127C – D0a, 128N – D0b, 128C – D1a, 129N – D1b, 129C – D2a, 130N – D3a, 130C – D4a, 131 – mixed common control, and (2) 126 – D-1c, 127N – D0c, 127C – D1c, 128N – D2b, 128C – D2c, 129N – D3b, 129C – D3c, 130N – D4b, 130C – D4c, 131 – mixed common control.  Phosphorylation Enrichment: The combined TMT labelled samples were enriched for phosphorylated peptides using a double titanium dioxide (TiOx) enrichment based on previously published methods (PMID: 25008320, PMID: 22906719). The final TiOx supernatant was retained for subsequent enrichment of “acetylated” peptides, and the elution was retained for “phosphorylated” peptide analysis.  Lysine Acetylation Enrichment: Following enrichment of phosphorylated peptides, the TiOx supernatant was subjected to lysine acetylation enrichment using the PTMScan® Acetyl-Lysine Motif [Ac-K] Kit (Product #13416, Cell Signaling Technology, Danvers, MA) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. The unbound fraction was retained for analysis of “non-modified” peptides, and the elution was retained for analysis of “acetylated” peptides.  High pH Reverse-Phase Fractionation: Both the “phosphorylated” and “non-modified” peptides were subjected to offline high pH reverse-phase fractionation as described below. Samples were resuspended in buffer A (20 mM ammonium formate, pH 9.3), and eluted over 97 min across a gradient of 2% to 50% buffer B (80% ACN, 20% buffer A), and collected in a concatenated fashion every 151 sec into a total of 20 fractions.  Mass Spectrometry: Each sample was analysed in biological triplicates. The peptides were captured on a commercial µ-precolumn (5µm, 5mm x 300 µm, 100 Å pore size, Acclaim PepMap 100 C18, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Bremen, Germany) before being separated using a home-packed column (1.9µm, 50cm x 100 µm, 120 Å pore size) of ReproSil-Pur C18 AQ beads (Dr. Maisch GmbH, Ammerbuch-Entringen, Germany) heated to 50°C, across a gradient of either; 8-45% buffer B (99.99% ACN, 0.01% FA) for 55 mins (“acetylated” and “non-modified” peptides) or 5-45% buffer B (99.99% ACN, 0.01% FA) for 55 mins (“phosphorylated” peptides), at 475nL/min with a Dionex UltiMate 3000 nanoLC system (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Reverse phase separated peptides were subsequently analysed by MS/MS using a Q Exactive HF-X Hybrid Quadrupole-Orbitrap Mass Spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific). A full MS scan with a mass range 350-1500 m/z was performed with a resolution of 120,000 and an AGC target of 3 x 106 ions, a maximum injection time of 50ms and a dynamic exclusion window of 20 sec. Fragmentation of the top 20 ions was performed on ions with a charge-state between +2 - +6 across a mass range of 350-1500 m/z, with a fixed first mass of 110 m/z, at a resolution of 45,000 with an AGC target of 1 x 105, a maximum injection time of 100ms, and a collision energy set at either 32 (“acetylated” and “non-modified” peptides) or 34 (“phosphorylated” peptides).
dataProcessingProtocol: Data were acquired using Xcalibur (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Generated data were analysed using Proteome Discoverer 2.3 and an in-house Mascot database server. The SwissProt database (updated 6th March 2020) filtered for human entries was used for identification. Data were searched with the following parameters; a precursor mass tolerance of 10 ppm, a fragment mass tolerance of 0.05 Da, trypsin digestion with a maximum of 4 missed cleavages, a fixed modification of Carbamidomethyl (C), and the following dynamic modifications: TMT6plex (K and N-term), Acetylation (K) and Phosphorylation (ST and Y). Quantification was performed by Proteome Discoverer with HCD MS/MS reporter ion integration within a 30 ppm window. Searches were filtered to a false discovery rate (FDR) of <1% using Percolator. The IMP-ptmRS node from Proteome Discoverer was used to calculate modification site localization probabilities and a 90% confidence threshold was applied.
